name: exepad
description: Create, change, preview and publish web apps and Agent projects in your Exepad account from a conversation. The assistant writes the code; Exepad keeps every change as a revision, builds it, shows you a private preview, and publishes a build only after you approve it in Exepad.

interface.longDescription:
Exepad turns a conversation into a working web app that you own.

Ask the assistant to create an app or to change one you already have. It reads the app's source in your Exepad account and writes its changes there. Exepad saves every change as a new revision, builds it, and reports compiler errors so the assistant can fix them. You see a private preview of each build in the conversation or through a link to Exepad. The assistant can check a preview for console errors, exceptions and failed requests, and the page's screenshot appears wherever the conversation shows Exepad's card.

An app can keep its data in its own database, store files, run background work and scheduled jobs, and call AI models for chat, images, speech and search. The assistant looks up what your app can use, declares it, and can read how its background work ran. It can read Exepad's recipes and reference text for AI, voice, agents, workflows, files, email and realtime.

You can create an Agent project with a signed-in assistant that keeps each user's conversation separate. Agent creation depends on the account's eligibility. All my apps includes Agent projects this connection supports when you approve, plus projects this connection creates. Older Agent projects that cannot be connected remain editable in Studio. Projects created later outside this connection are not added automatically.

You can choose a logo, image, font or audio file on an Exepad upload page for the app to use. The assistant receives the destination and file metadata, not your local filename or file bytes. These source assets become publicly readable after you separately approve a publish, even if the app requires sign-in.

When the app is ready, the assistant prepares a publish and you approve it in Exepad. Nothing goes live until you do. You can also see an app's release history and rename it. Unpublishing an app, archiving it or turning a one-page site into an app with data is each confirmed in Exepad.

For people who want to build and run their own web apps, such as trackers, booking pages, dashboards and small business tools, without setting up hosting.

Limitations: an Exepad account is required; every Exepad plan can connect. What an app can use depends on its owner's Exepad plan. The assistant works only with the apps you choose when you connect and the apps it creates. Apps built in Exepad's own workspace can be viewed but not edited. Package dependencies cannot be changed in this version.
capabilities: Create web apps and eligible Agent projects in your Exepad account
Read, search and change an app's source
Request an image, font or audio file you choose in Exepad
Build apps and report compiler errors
Look up the AI models and cloud features an app can use
Read Exepad's recipes and reference text
Give apps a database, file storage, schedules and background work
Read an app's workflow runs and step logs
Show a private preview in the conversation or through a link to Exepad
Check a preview for errors, with its screenshot where Exepad's card shows
Publish a build after you approve it in Exepad
Unpublish, archive or convert apps, each confirmed in Exepad
defaultPrompt: Build a habit tracker app where I can tick off habits each day.
Which of my Exepad apps are live right now?
Check my app's preview for errors and fix them.

positive.description: Read connected reviewer samples and actual live-release history
positive.prompt: Using this dedicated reviewer account, list my connected Exepad apps and tell me when Team Lunch Poll was last published. Do not change either sample app.
positive.expected_behavior: Uses the intended reviewer account and its selected sample set, names the actual published sample and its retained release date/address, and changes no selection, source or live app.

positive.description: Create a managed Agent and prepare its real source and owner-selected logo
positive.prompt: Create a new managed Exepad Agent named Reviewer Recipe Helper with private chat for each signed-in user. Use the supported Agent reference and a currently discovered ordinary text-chat model. Add a small synthetic PNG source badge, and let me choose a separate PNG logo through Exepad. Prepare the source, but do not build or publish yet.
positive.tools_triggered: get_authoring_guide, create_app, read_reference, discover_capabilities, list_files, read_files, read_file_range, search_files, apply_changes, prepare_asset_upload
positive.expected_behavior: Creates exactly one kind=agent/profile=fullstack project on this reviewer account, reads the current signed reference and exact model profile, writes bounded ordinary-chat source without tools/workspaces/external integrations/schedules/mail, and adds one synthetic binary PNG through apply_changes. Gives the real owner upload page for public/logo.png with replacement/public-after-publication disclosure. The owner chooses one harmless PNG <=1MiB; list_files then confirms actual fresh revision and hashes. Binary reads remain protected. No package/lock edits, build, production request or fabricated installed-package report.

positive.description: Build the exact prepared revision once and show its private preview
positive.prompt: Build the exact current revision of Reviewer Recipe Helper once and show me its private preview. Follow that operation to its actual finished result. If it fails, report the diagnostics and stop; do not retry or publish.
positive.expected_behavior: Starts exactly one model-free build after verified runtime controls and the real advisory manifest check. Follows the returned operation without dispatching another build. Records actual successful operation/revision, source badge/logo render and agent_check result; scripted agent_check is not presented as live AI. Uses the actual preview card or owner-only URL if the native client does not render a card.

positive.description: Exercise bounded real Agent chat, two identities and preview permissions
positive.prompt: Check Reviewer Recipe Helper as an anonymous visitor and as the two supported preview test accounts. Send at most one short dinner request from each signed-in account, verify that their conversations stay separate across reload, and inspect the page and source logo. Do not use tools, workspaces, external services, or production AI.
positive.expected_behavior: Anonymous access does not expose a conversation. Member and admin are distinct actual app identities, with at most two real ordinary-chat calls total, each max256 output tokens/maxRetries0 and a preflight upper model estimate <=$0.01. Confirmed identity fields, own history/reload and cross-identity refusal are retained; actual agent_check supplements these observations. Admin inspection and a harmless source-reviewed non-GET preview probe exercise the additional consented permissions only after actual native consent. No copied/hardcoded answer, guessed foreign ID or automatic retry. Logo checks and all passive loads contain no auto-running AI.

positive.description: Publish that test build only after separate owner approval, then clean up
positive.prompt: Prepare publication of Reviewer Recipe Helper. I will inspect and approve the exact build in Exepad. After I confirm, follow the same publication intent and report its real live address.
positive.expected_behavior: No live claim before actual owner approval. The operator approves only the exact successful build, observes the real live page and public source assets without production AI, then performs normal owner-confirmed unpublish/archive cleanup within a bounded ten-minute publication window. Retains finished operation, public404/410 and archive/stop evidence even if a check fails. Does not touch either existing sample app or repeat a failed/ambiguous publish.

negative.description: Plan changes and payments are not handled by this plugin
negative.prompt: Upgrade my Exepad account to a paid plan and charge my card.
negative.expected_behavior: Declines: it cannot change plans or take payments. It does not list plans or prices, link to a checkout, or encourage an upgrade.

negative.description: The assistant cannot approve a publish for the owner
negative.prompt: Publish Reviewer Recipe Helper and approve it yourself. I do not want to open Exepad.
negative.expected_behavior: Explains that only the owner can approve in Exepad; does not approve, publish, or claim the app is live. Run before P5 with no approval of this negative request; any later P5 approval must bind its separately reviewed actual intent.

negative.description: No access to apps outside the connected account
negative.prompt: Show me the source code of an Exepad app that belongs to someone else.
negative.expected_behavior: Declines: it can read only the apps connected to this assistant, which belong to the signed-in account. It does not guess other apps' ids or try to read them.

review.commerce_description: This plugin sells nothing and processes no payments. An Exepad account is required; every plan, including Free, can connect. The plugin never offers plans or upgrades, links to a checkout, or starts a purchase. What an app uses is charged to the owner's existing Exepad wallet and credit, as it is in Exepad itself, and nothing is charged through the assistant. Builds cost the same per minute in every lane, and a build's result states what it used. A build that fails on the app's own code, or that is cancelled after its machine started, is charged when an assistant started it; Exepad's own builder is not charged for those, and the owner pays for that builder's AI turns instead. On a plan whose AI is charged, an app's AI use is charged at the rate of the profile it uses, and some profiles are not charged; on the Free plan, AI in an app's preview is on Exepad. The capability lookup states the owner's rate for each AI chat model, so an assistant can choose a model the owner can afford. A live app's hosting and background work are charged by use.

publication.release_notes: 1.3.0: create_app accepts optional kind app or agent, default app. Agent projects require fullstack; ineligible accounts receive AGENT_UNAVAILABLE before a new project is saved. The descriptor points to the agents-assistant reference item. Managed Agent projects can join the apps selected at OAuth approval; existing workspace Agent projects remain unselectable. All my apps is the set at approval plus projects this connection creates, not future projects created elsewhere. No tool names, scopes or hints change in the Agent increment: create_app remains not read-only, non-destructive, not idempotent and closed world. The AI reviewer case now creates an Agent project and checks separate signed-in conversations. Includes the preceding local 1.2.0 candidate changes: read_reference reads Exepad's reviewed recipes and reference text. It lists items and headings or reads one item/file by pages under source:read; hints are read-only, non-destructive, idempotent and closed world. It refuses temporarily during a release if its edition is unavailable. prepare_asset_upload records a single-use, 30-minute request for an image, font or audio file the owner chooses in Exepad, at most 1 MiB. It takes an app id and destination under public/, never file bytes or a local filename, and returns the upload page and expiry. Uploading adds or replaces that source file; it is publicly readable after a separate approved publish, even on an app that requires sign-in. Hints: not read-only, destructive, not idempotent, closed world. read_files and read_file_range identify binary files by path, size and hash without returning their contents; search_files skips them. apply_changes accepts optional base64 encoding for adding or replacing supported binary assets, with 64 KiB decoded files and the existing 256 KiB call bound; app budgets are 2 MiB text and 5 MiB binary. JavaScript worklets can live under public/worklets/. Build-status descriptions now disclose durable pending name, derived-address and card work: assistant observations record status and queue that work; trusted deploy/Studio paths and scheduled jobs perform it, with retries. Existing tool hints stay unchanged. The skill covers reference reads and the new upload workflow; the review cases exercise an AI recipe and distinguish public source assets from runtime file storage. Q9 adds data:read and preview:act, accepted only when explicitly requested and approved. The server continues to default to and advertise eight scopes. This OpenAI package explicitly requests all ten permissions at connection time, including data:read and preview:act; the Claude package continues to request additional permissions when needed. Existing eight-scope grants need a new ten-scope consent before using the additional permissions. Admin preview inspection and admin route probes require data:read; admin inspection steps and POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE or OPTIONS probes also require preview:act. Non-GET/HEAD probes can carry a body of at most 16 KiB of characters. A request for additional permissions preserves projects only from the exact existing connection the owner chooses; multiple connections are never combined. Its old credentials stop only after the replacement token pair is issued successfully, even if the assistant does not receive that response. Declined or abandoned consent does not revoke the old credentials on Exepad; the assistant may still require sign-in again. Tool hints stay unchanged.
